evals.name: eval-0-readme-rewrite
evals.prompt: This README reads like a bot wrote it. Clean it up.
evals.expected_output: A README in Google devdocs style: sentence-case headings, second person, present tense, active voice, no filler words, descriptive link text, every technical fact preserved.
assertions: No filler or belittling words (simply, just, easily, in order to, utilize, e.g., note that)
Addresses the reader in second person rather than 'we'
Uses present tense, not future ('will be generated')
Preserves every technical fact (commands, env var, flags, layout, Node version)

evals.name: eval-1-error-messages
evals.prompt: Our CLI error messages are useless when something breaks. Reword them.
evals.expected_output: Error strings that say what happened and what to do next, with no exclamation points, blame, apologies, double negatives, or ableist terms. File stays valid TypeScript with identical keys.
assertions: Keeps every exported key and the file's TypeScript shape
Replaces violent or ableist terms (sanity check, insane, abort)
Most messages tell the reader what to do next (>=70%)

evals.name: eval-2-agent-instructions
evals.prompt: Tidy up the CLAUDE.md for this project.
evals.expected_output: An agent instruction file in sentence case, timeless (no 'currently'/'new'), free of filler, with every original rule and technical fact intact.
assertions: Timeless: no 'currently', 'at this time', or 'new' as novelty
Preserves every rule and technical fact
